title: Boundary and single-color insertion identities for ordered join chains
statement:
Let $r\geq1$, let $I=\{0,\ldots,r-1\}$, and let $X_i$ be sets with specified $v_i\in X_i$ for $i\in I$. For each integer $q$, let $J_q$ be the free abelian group with specified $\mathbf Z$-basis in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-free-module] consisting of symbols $[(i_0,x_0),\ldots,(i_q,x_q)]$ with $i_0<\cdots<i_q$ in $I$ and $x_a\in X_{i_a}$ when $0\leq q<r$. Let $J_{-1}=\mathbf Z[\varnothing]$ with its empty-symbol basis, and let $J_q=0$ in all other degrees. Define degree-one homomorphisms $c_i$ by zero on symbols containing $i$ and by inserting $(i,v_i)$ with sign $(-1)^k$ on symbols missing $i$, where $k$ counts colors less than $i$. Define degree-zero $R_i$ by zero on symbols missing $i$ and by $R_i\sigma=\sigma-T_i\sigma$ otherwise, where $T_i$ replaces the color-$i$ vertex by $(i,v_i)$. All formulas are extended by integer linearity, and all components involving zero source or target groups are zero. Define $d_q:J_q\to J_{q-1}$ by alternating deletion, with sign $(-1)^a$ for deletion of zero-based position $a$; thus $d_0[(i,x)]=[\varnothing]$ and $d_{-1}=0$. Then, for every integer $q$ and every $i\in I$,
$$d_{q-1}d_q=0,\qquad d_{q+1}c_{i,q}+c_{i,q-1}d_q=\operatorname{id}_{J_q}-R_{i,q}.$$
These identities include degree $-1$, degree $r-1$, and the zero groups outside $[-1,r-1]$; no equality between any $x_a$ and any chosen vertex $v_i$ is assumed.

proof.text: By [def-weil-pbc-free-module], every chain has a unique finite integer expansion in the specified symbols. Each displayed basis assignment has a finite output: deletion has at most $q+1$ terms, insertion at most one, and replacement at most two. Extending by $\sum_\sigma a_\sigma\sigma\mapsto\sum_\sigma a_\sigma f(\sigma)$ therefore defines homomorphisms. Both requested identities are equalities of homomorphisms, so it suffices to check the basis symbols in each nonzero degree.

proof.text: For a symbol $\sigma$ of degree $q\geq1$, write $\sigma_{\widehat a,\widehat b}$ for deletion of its original positions $a<b$. Deleting $a$ first and then the shifted position $b-1$ contributes $(-1)^{a+b-1}\sigma_{\widehat a,\widehat b}$ to $d_{q-1}d_q\sigma$; deleting $b$ first and then $a$ contributes $(-1)^{a+b}\sigma_{\widehat a,\widehat b}$. Every term occurs in exactly one such pair, whose coefficients add to zero. Thus $d^2\sigma=0$, including $q=1$, where the final symbol is empty. In degree $0$ or $-1$ the composite contains $d_{-1}=0$; all other source groups are zero.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent-written ordered-join expansion below local continuous-cocycle descent, calculations 1-4; these elementary calculations are not asserted in the blueprint.

proof.text: Suppose $i$ is missing from a symbol $\sigma$, and put $k=\#\{j\text{ a color of }\sigma:j<i\}$. In $dc_i\sigma$, deletion of the inserted vertex has coefficient $(-1)^{k+k}=1$ and leaves $\sigma$. For an original position $a<k$, its deletion in $dc_i\sigma$ has coefficient $(-1)^{k+a}$, whereas deletion followed by insertion in $c_id\sigma$ has coefficient $(-1)^{a+k-1}$. For an original position $a\geq k$, the two coefficients are $(-1)^{k+a+1}$ and $(-1)^{a+k}$. In each pair the output symbol is identical and the coefficients cancel. Hence $(dc_i+c_id)\sigma=\sigma=(1-R_i)\sigma$, since $R_i\sigma=0$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent-written ordered-join expansion below local continuous-cocycle descent, calculations 1-4; these elementary calculations are not asserted in the blueprint.

proof.text: Suppose $i$ occurs at position $k$ of $\sigma$. Then $c_i\sigma=0$. Every boundary face other than deletion of position $k$ still contains $i$, so insertion on it is zero. The face deleting position $k$ has coefficient $(-1)^k$ and reinsertion at the same position has coefficient $(-1)^k$, giving $c_id\sigma=T_i\sigma$. Consequently $(dc_i+c_id)\sigma=T_i\sigma=\sigma-(\sigma-T_i\sigma)=(1-R_i)\sigma$. This calculation does not require the original color-$i$ vertex to differ from $v_i$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent-written ordered-join expansion below local continuous-cocycle descent, calculations 1-4; these elementary calculations are not asserted in the blueprint.

proof.text: In degree $-1$, $c_i[\varnothing]=[(i,v_i)]$, so $d_0c_i[\varnothing]=[\varnothing]$, while $c_id_{-1}=0$ and $R_i[\varnothing]=0$. In degree $r-1$ every color occurs, so the preceding present-color calculation applies, with $c_i=0$ into $J_r=0$. In every degree outside $[-1,r-1]$ all maps in either identity have zero source. Thus the formulas hold in every integer degree. For $r=1$ these are precisely the empty and singleton calculations. Linearity as in step 1 gives both identities on all chains.

lean.statement: theorem singleColorIdentities (r : ℕ) (hr : 1 ≤ r) (X : Fin r → Type u) (v : ∀ i : Fin r, X i) : (∀ q : ℤ, (boundary X (q - 1) (q - 2)).comp (boundary X q (q - 1)) = 0) ∧ (∀ (q : ℤ) (i : Fin r), (boundary X (q + 1) q).comp (insertion v i q (q + 1)) + (insertion v i (q - 1) q).comp (boundary X q (q - 1)) = LinearMap.id - remainder v i q)
